Test Case: SHEET-GAP-03 Parent/child overlap winner

Test Case: SHEET-GAP-10 Turning base Express back ON does not revive a canceled event
Test data / Preconditions: A normal Express-ON QA KML with active degradation; ability to toggle base Express OFF and ON; record its actual service-area name, internal KML ID and base SLA.
Steps: Apply +15 to the normal Express-ON KML; turn base Express OFF for it, then turn it back ON without submitting another degradation. Read the effective state; use a new Add only as a separate control.
Expected: Base OFF cancels the active event; turning Express back ON restores the base state but does not revive the canceled event. Only a newly accepted Add creates a new degradation.

Test Case: DB-01 Final schema and index verification
Test data / Preconditions: Final SQL schema deployed in isolated QA; engineer SQL metadata access; target environment and DB build recorded.
Steps: Inspect CREATE TABLE output and indexes for slots_config_kml_wise, kml_degradation_event and bulk_operation_tracking; compare types, keys and nullability with the LLD.
Expected: slots_config_kml_wise keeps express, sla_minutes and fulfillment_sla as base values and uses uq_slots_kml_id. kml_degradation_event includes BIGINT auto-increment id, kml_id matching the base type/collation, nullable parent_id, operation_id, action_type ADD/EDIT/REMOVE, extent INT >= 0, express_off and is_current TINYINT 0/1, UTC DATETIME(3) start_time/end_time/created_at, source MANUAL/AUTO, reason and created_by. Indexes are (kml_id,id), (kml_id,is_current), UNIQUE(operation_id,kml_id), plus functional uniqueness for kml_id only when is_current=1; do not use UNIQUE(kml_id,is_current). bulk_operation_tracking stores one row per operation/city with PENDING/COMPLETED/FAILED status, timestamps, action, actor, reason, JSON hub_ids and requested settings; primary key (operation_id,city_id), index (status,updated_at).

Test Case: DB-03 Per-city operation tracking records
Test data / Preconditions: QA database access; one operation targeting at least two cities; operation includes requested-setting metadata.
Steps: Submit one multi-city ADD or REMOVE through the UI; inspect bulk_operation_tracking rows and compare them with operation details and city progress before and after consumption.
Expected: There is one tracking row per operation/city with a shared operation ID and a composite (operation_id,city_id) key. Status transitions use PENDING, COMPLETED or FAILED. Optional unknown metadata remains NULL; REMOVE has no requested extent/end time. hub_ids records the admission scope when known. COMPLETED means city SQL work committed, including when targets were skipped; there is no persisted per-KML result.

Test Case: DB-05 Lock order and concurrent base writes
Test data / Preconditions: Disposable KML fixtures; engineer-controlled concurrent Add, base Express OFF, base SLA edit, soft delete and stale Edit operations; SQL lock visibility.
Steps: Race queued Add against base Express OFF and soft deletion; separately race Add with base SLA edit and a synchronous Edit. Observe lock acquisition, state rereads and final SQL/event state.
Expected: Consumer locks the operation/city row first, then base rows in ascending KML-ID order through uq_slots_kml_id, and rereads eligibility/current state after locking. Base OFF plus cancellation commits atomically; base-OFF or deleted targets are not revived. Base writes serialize. A later consumed Add may supersede a synchronous Edit according to partition/lock order.

Test Case: KAFKA-02 Same-city ordering and partition behavior
Test data / Preconditions: Isolated targets in one city and another city; access to broker topic, partition, offset and consumer logs.
Steps: Queue Add, Remove and Add for the same city, then submit work for a different city. Correlate UI submission, broker partition/offset, consumed order and final database state.
Expected: Observed ordering follows broker partition order, not assumed UI click time. Processing is sequential within a partition. cityId is the message key but cities can share a partition, so unrelated cities may block each other. No Redis city lock or dedicated partition per city is assumed.

Test Case: KAFKA-03 Command without a tracking row cannot execute
Test data / Preconditions: Isolated command with no matching operation/city row in the primary bulk_operation_tracking table; broker and SQL observation access.
Steps: Deliver the command whose operation/city tracking row is absent. Inspect consumer outcome, event/current-marker tables, analytics output and acknowledgement/retry logs.
Expected: A command without its matching tracking row cannot execute or create an event/analytics record. It cannot mark a nonexistent operation/city as completed. Record the consumer handling outcome from the deployed contract.

Test Case: KAFKA-04 Acknowledge only after commit outcome is known
Test data / Preconditions: Controlled uncertain SQL commit or lost broker acknowledgement; primary SQL tracking access; broker acknowledgement logs.
Steps: Allow a command to reach an uncertain commit boundary and simulate a lost acknowledgement. Inspect the primary tracking row before any resume, then observe broker acknowledgement and final event state.
Expected: Resolve uncertainty from the primary tracking row before re-execution. A committed event is not applied twice; a terminal tracking result is not overwritten; acknowledge only after the durable outcome is known. If the outcome remains uncertain, delivery stays retryable.

Test Case: KAFKA-06 Malformed command versus infrastructure failure
Test data / Preconditions: Controlled malformed envelope and positively malformed Avro payload, plus separate schema-registry, network, authentication and SQL outage scenarios.
Steps: Deliver each failure class independently. Inspect retry, discard, acknowledgement, tracking status and whether any SQL event or analytics record was created.
Expected: Invalid envelopes are rejected according to the command contract. Only positively identified malformed Avro follows the bounded retry-and-skip policy. Schema, network, authentication and uncertain SQL failures remain retryable and are not treated as harmless malformed payloads. A skipped or acknowledged poison message is never reported as committed SQL success.

Test Case: KAFKA-07 Analytics publication timing and reconciliation
Test data / Preconditions: Successful ADD, EDIT, REMOVE, AUTO and base-OFF cancellation fixtures; skipped, rolled-back, expired and redelivered cases; SQL and analytics topic access.
Steps: Compare inserted SQL events with DEGRADATION_EVENT_V2 records. Simulate analytics publisher failure or crash and an ambiguous retry; reconcile the topic with SQL.
Expected: Publish after SQL commit, once per inserted ADD/EDIT/REMOVE including AUTO and base-OFF cancellation. Do not publish for expiry, skipped targets, rollback, marker-only changes or terminal redelivery. Analytics is best effort and may lose or duplicate events; deduplicate by degradationId and reconcile against SQL. Schema version 1 uses epoch-millisecond timestamps, numeric long IDs, integer expressOff and no null fields.

Test data / Preconditions: Isolated accepted Add, OFF and Remove operations; QA KML EventBus client settings, service identity and correlation ID; broker/EventBus request and response logs.
Steps: Capture the original emitted KML_DEGRADATION_COMMAND and POST /api/v1/events/individual request. Verify headers, schema fields and time units for explicit and city-wide commands, OFF and Remove; inspect response mapping and resulting consumer outcome.

Test Case: KAFKA-11 Bounded queue saturation and rejected dispatch
Test data / Preconditions: Controlled admission executor saturation and analytics executor saturation; record deployed queue capacities, rejection policy, watchdog threshold and relevant logs/metrics.
Steps: Fill each queue to its configured limit in isolated QA. Submit command work during admission saturation; separately commit SQL events during analytics saturation. Inspect HTTP/operation outcome, tracking rows, SQL state, retry/reconciliation and rejection/publish metrics.
Expected: Observed behavior matches the deployed bounded-queue policy. Saturation must not report a city as SQL-completed without a committed transaction; persisted Pending work follows the documented watchdog/recovery path and reaches a known terminal outcome. Analytics saturation cannot roll back SQL and is reconciled as best-effort loss/duplicate behavior. Record actual limits; do not assume the default capacity.
